To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status:** Privileged and confidential. Internal negotiation advice.

I have treated the Seller's covering note and its "fair and balanced" description as advocacy, not as agreed positions. Nearly every headline position departs from our playbook. Several departures are hidden in drafting rather than stated openly.

---

## 1. Threshold point: fallbacks are not available

The Seller has proposed exactly our two conditional fallbacks: a **20% / AUD 4.8m cap** and an **18-month claims period**. That may be coincidence or informed anchoring. Either way:

- **No written authority from Amelia Frost exists** for either fallback, for this draft or any other.
- The team must **not** signal flexibility, accept, or "park" either point. We should not hint that we have room to move until Amelia gives specific written authority identifying the draft.
- Our response should restate 25% / AUD 6.0m and 24 months as our position.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture (highest priority)

**1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m**
- *Playbook:* 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is unauthorised.
- *Pushback:* Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**
- *Seller:* AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, excess only.
- *Playbook:* AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- The Seller's de minimis is 5x ours and its basket is 5x ours. The "excess only" (deductible) mechanism permanently strips AUD 250k from every recovery.
- *Pushback:* Reject all three elements. The de minimis should also not apply to aggregated related claims. Consider a deeming rule so that related or recurring matters count together.

**3. Claims period (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months**
- *Playbook:* 24 months. 18 months is unauthorised.
- *Pushback:* Reject. Restore 24 months.

**4. Hidden override (cl 12.3 / 13): "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"**
- This is a general-regime sweep. Its practical effect is to pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims into the general caps, thresholds and time limits by default. It conflicts with our playbook rule that categories stay separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- *Pushback:* Delete. Reverse the default. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, as expressly defined. Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, price/payment and covenant claims each need their own regime.

**5. Fundamental / Title folded into the general regime**
- The Seller offers "administrative simplicity" as the reason. That is not a legal rationale.
- Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. A 20% cap on a title failure is commercially untenable.
- *Pushback:* Reject. Fundamental/Title claims need:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a period of at least six years;
  - exclusion from the general basket, the de minimis and any knowledge bar.

**6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature"**
- As drafted, this would cover **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. Our playbook says these are carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive that.
- *Pushback:* Non-negotiable. Insert an overriding carve-out stating that no limitation applies to claims arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers. "No limitation" here covers caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers. The non-reliance clause must not purport to exclude liability for fraudulent misrepresentation or misleading or deceptive conduct where exclusion is not enforceable.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**7. General disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)**
- The Seller deems disclosed everything in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." That is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook tells us to reject.
- It is made worse by DL 1.4, which says nothing admits breach, materiality or that any consent or notice is required. In other words, the Seller wants the protection of disclosure without committing to what the disclosed facts mean.
- **Timing gap:** the data-room cut-off is **5.00pm 22 September 2026**, and today is 5 November 2026. That is roughly six weeks old.
- *Pushback:*
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Only specific disclosures in the letter count.
  - Those disclosures must be **fair**: enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and the warranty it qualifies.
  - The data room may be referenced only where a specific document is identified against a specific warranty.
  - No disclosure may qualify Title, capacity, Tax or IP fundamentals, specific indemnities, or fraud.
  - Require a refreshed data-room index and an updated disclosure position as at signing, with any Completion bring-down controlled by us. Supplementary disclosure must not cure breaches without our consent.

**8. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)**
- The clause bars claims on anything known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is a blanket exclusion. It is wider than actual knowledge and effectively reintroduces the deemed-disclosure regime.
- *Pushback:* Delete. If any qualifier survives, limit it to the actual (not constructive) knowledge of named Buyer individuals. Our playbook focus is the other side of this: any **Seller** knowledge qualifier on warranties must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. A knowledge bar must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Deal-specific risk items

**9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2)**
- Bluefen is about **30% of FY26 revenue** (about AUD 3.6m). This is a material customer.
- The Seller offers only reasonable endeavours, with the condition satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- DL 2 confirms that **no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** have been provided.
- Consent-on-delivery is the playbook's specific failure mode. A consent letter can be delivered while the cl 11.3 conditions remain unmet, leaving the consent ineffective or conditional.
- *Pushback:* Make it a Condition Precedent requiring:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2;
  - documentary evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion;
  - a Buyer-only waiver right;
  - a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours (for example, all reasonable endeavours, or best endeavours, with defined actions);
  - Buyer participation in communications with Bluefen;
  - a long-stop date and a termination right.

**10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3)**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller proposes a release **following** Completion.
- That would leave the security attached to a business we own, and a possible change-of-control default, with our only protection being a post-completion promise.
- *Pushback:* Require:
  - a current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, including per diem amounts;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, with the amount deducted in the price mechanics as Debt;
  - executed security releases, deeds of release and PPSR discharge documents delivered at Completion.
- *Fallback (Amelia's approval required, not available now):* a post-completion release supported by Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout. Do not offer this.

**11. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)**
- The Seller states the AUD 420k DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- The bonuses are triggered by Completion and are payable by the Company as employer. Unless they are funded or deducted, the cost falls on us after Completion. The words "matter for the Seller" have no mechanical effect in a funds flow.
- *Pushback:* Either:
  - add a specific line item, so the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs are paid through payroll at Completion and deducted from the price; or
  - include them in the Debt definition, with an express Seller indemnity for any residual amounts.
- Also require the Seller to quantify the on-costs and to confirm the treatment of any continued-employment amounts that vest after Completion.

**12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- The risk is therefore broader than a payment dispute. It extends to ownership of IP the business may rely on, and to infringement or third-party claims.
- *Pushback:*
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials and related deliverables.
  - Preserve the cure route: pay the outstanding SOW3 fees (Seller-funded or deducted) and obtain a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.
- *Caution on the number:* DL 4 states, and we should accept, that the **AUD 180k in DD-010 is not independently verified**, either as paid or unpaid. Require Ironquay or bank confirmation, and do not fix the indemnity at AUD 180k.

**13. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." We should not accept that conclusion. We should equally not assert the opposite.
- The record shows a download link sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification obligation are **unestablished**.
- We should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach. We should not assert harm, a Notifiable Data Breaches duty or a loss figure. No numeric demand should be made on the current facts.
- *Pushback:* Covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation, with any assessment of whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) carried out properly and on time;
  - give regular written updates and copies of the findings before Completion;
  - consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator contact.
- Also seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations, with the amount left open. The Seller's materiality statement should not be repeated in the SPA.

**14. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**
- There are three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total). The Seller labels them ordinary-course costs. DL 8 itself concedes it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Our approach:* Assess, do not presume. Request the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts, the timing, the scope, the termination rights, any accrual and the business rationale. Find out whether the renewals were entered into in contemplation of the sale.
- Do **not** reflexively classify them as Debt or demand a price deduction. Reserve the position pending the facts, and include appropriate conduct-of-business covenants and warranties.

**15. Tax / IP regime**
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **open**.
- *Pushback:* Reject the characterisation. Reserve the Tax and IP regimes (caps, periods, any tax indemnity) for separate negotiation.
- Internally, assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution.

**16. Title (DL 10)**
- The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal document supplied by the Seller. DL 10 itself concedes it is not verification.
- *Pushback:* Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates, or confirmation that none exist;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement, with pre-emption and drag/tag waivers;
  - a PPSR search, encumbrance releases (tie this to Riverlark), and confirmation of no options, convertibles or share issues;
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority and capacity.
- The register should not be used as a substitute for a title warranty or a basis for disclosure against it.

### D. Lower-priority items: verify, do not overstate

**17. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The disclosure describes a lease notification obligation and an assignment restriction, but does not say that consent is triggered by a share sale.
- Verify by reviewing the actual clauses for change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.
- If notification only, make it a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable.
- Do not inflate these into Conditions Precedent unless review shows a consent requirement.

---

## 3. Recommendations summary

**Reject outright and restate our position**
1. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m**. The 20% fallback has not been authorised.
2. Thresholds: **AUD 5k de minimis / AUD 50k basket**, recoverable from the first dollar.
3. General claims period: **24 months**. The 18-month fallback has not been authorised.
4. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override. Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate.
5. Fundamental/Title: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**: carved out of every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision. Not negotiable and not waivable.
7. Delete general and deemed disclosure. Require specific, fair disclosure and a refreshed disclosure position, because the 22 September cut-off is stale.
8. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.

**Strengthen into Conditions Precedent or Completion deliverables**
9. Bluefen: effective consent **plus evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions** as a Buyer-waivable Condition Precedent, with stronger than reasonable endeavours.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and releases at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia's approval and an irrevocable undertaking.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k **plus on-costs** as an explicit funds-flow line item or Debt, deducted or Seller-funded.
12. Title: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Negotiate or investigate**
13. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
14. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants, plus an open-amount specific indemnity. Assume no confirmed breach.
15. Sandbar: request information and assess. No automatic Debt classification.
16. Tax and IP: record them as open. Reject "settled."
17. Lease and Mossvale: verify the clause wording, and handle any notice as a covenant.

**Internal actions**
- Do not concede the cap or the claims period until Amelia Frost gives written authority specific to this draft.
- Request now: the Bluefen cl 11.3 evidence, a Riverlark payout figure, the DD-005 on-cost calculation, Ironquay payment confirmation, the DD-006 investigation status, the Sandbar contracts, and the title documents.
- Respond with a full mark-up rather than a points list. Several of the Seller's concessions-by-drafting (the cl 12.3 override, cl 8.3, the cl 20.5 reach, DL 1.1–1.2) would be easy to miss in a summary negotiation.

- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller proposes a release **following** Completion.
- That would leave the security attached to a business we own, and a possible change-of-control default, with our only protection being a post-completion promise.
- *Pushback:* Require:
  - a current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, including per diem amounts;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, with the amount deducted in the price mechanics as Debt;
  - executed security releases, deeds of release and PPSR discharge documents delivered at Completion.
- *Fallback (Amelia's approval required, not available now):* a post-completion release supported by Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout. Do not offer this.

**11. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)**
- The Seller states the AUD 420k DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- The bonuses are triggered by Completion and are payable by the Company as employer. Unless they are funded or deducted, the cost falls on us after Completion. The words "matter for the Seller" have no mechanical effect in a funds flow.
- *Pushback:* Either:
  - add a specific line item, so the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs are paid through payroll at Completion and deducted from the price; or
  - include them in the Debt definition, with an express Seller indemnity for any residual amounts.
- Also require the Seller to quantify the on-costs and to confirm the treatment of any continued-employment amounts that vest after Completion.

**12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- The risk is therefore broader than a payment dispute. It extends to ownership of IP the business may rely on, and to infringement or third-party claims.
- *Pushback:*
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials and related deliverables.
  - Preserve the cure route: pay the outstanding SOW3 fees (Seller-funded or deducted) and obtain a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.
- *Caution on the number:* DL 4 states, and we should accept, that the **AUD 180k in DD-010 is not independently verified**, either as paid or unpaid. Require Ironquay or bank confirmation, and do not fix the indemnity at AUD 180k.

**13. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." We should not accept that conclusion. We should equally not assert the opposite.
- The record shows a download link sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification obligation are **unestablished**.
- We should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach. We should not assert harm, a Notifiable Data Breaches duty or a loss figure. No numeric demand should be made on the current facts.
- *Pushback:* Covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation, with any assessment of whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) carried out properly and on time;
  - give regular written updates and copies of the findings before Completion;
  - consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator contact.
- Also seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations, with the amount left open. The Seller's materiality statement should not be repeated in the SPA.

**14. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**
- There are three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total). The Seller labels them ordinary-course costs. DL 8 itself concedes it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Our approach:* Assess, do not presume. Request the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts, the timing, the scope, the termination rights, any accrual and the business rationale. Find out whether the renewals were entered into in contemplation of the sale.
- Do **not** reflexively classify them as Debt or demand a price deduction. Reserve the position pending the facts, and include appropriate conduct-of-business covenants and warranties.

**15. Tax / IP regime**
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **open**.
- *Pushback:* Reject the characterisation. Reserve the Tax and IP regimes (caps, periods, any tax indemnity) for separate negotiation.
- Internally, assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution.

**16. Title (DL 10)**
- The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal document supplied by the Seller. DL 10 itself concedes it is not verification.
- *Pushback:* Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates, or confirmation that none exist;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement, with pre-emption and drag/tag waivers;
  - a PPSR search, encumbrance releases (tie this to Riverlark), and confirmation of no options, convertibles or share issues;
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority and capacity.
- The register should not be used as a substitute for a title warranty or a basis for disclosure against it.

### D. Lower-priority items: verify, do not overstate

**17. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The disclosure describes a lease notification obligation and an assignment restriction, but does not say that consent is triggered by a share sale.
- Verify by reviewing the actual clauses for change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.
- If notification only, make it a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable.
- Do not inflate these into Conditions Precedent unless review shows a consent requirement.

## 3. Recommendations summary

**Reject outright and restate our position**
1. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m**. The 20% fallback has not been authorised.
2. Thresholds: **AUD 5k de minimis / AUD 50k basket**, recoverable from the first dollar.
3. General claims period: **24 months**. The 18-month fallback has not been authorised.
4. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override. Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate.
5. Fundamental/Title: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**: carved out of every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision. Not negotiable and not waivable.
7. Delete general and deemed disclosure. Require specific, fair disclosure and a refreshed disclosure position, because the 22 September cut-off is stale.
8. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.

**Strengthen into Conditions Precedent or Completion deliverables**
9. Bluefen: effective consent **plus evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions** as a Buyer-waivable Condition Precedent, with stronger than reasonable endeavours.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and releases at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia's approval and an irrevocable undertaking.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k **plus on-costs** as an explicit funds-flow line item or Debt, deducted or Seller-funded.
12. Title: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Negotiate or investigate**
13. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
14. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants, plus an open-amount specific indemnity. Assume no confirmed breach.
15. Sandbar: request information and assess. No automatic Debt classification.
16. Tax and IP: record them as open. Reject "settled."
17. Lease and Mossvale: verify the clause wording, and handle any notice as a covenant.

**Internal actions**
- Do not concede the cap or the claims period until Amelia Frost gives written authority specific to this draft.
- Request now: the Bluefen cl 11.3 evidence, a Riverlark payout figure, the DD-005 on-cost calculation, Ironquay payment confirmation, the DD-006 investigation status, the Sandbar contracts, and the title documents.
- Respond with a full mark-up rather than a points list. Several of the Seller's concessions-by-drafting (the cl 12.3 override, cl 8.3, the cl 20.5 reach, DL 1.1–1.2) would be easy to miss in a summary negotiation.
